q2.title: Is the session-name to work_id inverse unambiguous for multi-segment work ids?
q2.imperative: fact: read run_crew.session_name and confirm the grammar; state whether gate/role/attempt can ever contain a slash.
q2.finding: FACT. run_crew.py:83-88 session_name() = 'constellation/<work_id>/<gate>/<role>/attempt-<n>'. gate ids (g1-implement), roles (implementer/reviewer) and 'attempt-N' never contain '/', so the inverse IS unambiguous: work_id = '/'.join(parts[1:-3]) after asserting parts[0]=='constellation', len(parts)>=5, parts[-1].startswith('attempt-'). The current code takes parts[1] only (run_crew.py:936-939).

q3.title: Which run_crew code paths are affected: launch or only recovery?
q3.imperative: fact: trace argparse handling of --work-id vs --verify-result/--resume/--abandon.
q3.finding: FACT. Only the RECOVERY paths re-parse. Launch passes args.work_id straight through (run_crew.py:864-865 load_registry(registry_path(args.work_id, root))). load_registry_for_resume is called from THREE sites: --verify-result (824), --resume (848), bare --abandon (867). So one shared parse fix repairs all three; the issue names only --verify-result because that is the path epic-659/665 exercised.

q4.title: How exactly does verify_agent_feedback break, and which of its other work_id uses are slash-safe?
q4.imperative: fact: read _current_run_archive_dirs and every other work_id use in the module.
q4.finding: FACT. verify_agent_feedback.py:72-80 _current_run_archive_dirs iterates archive_root.iterdir() (depth 1 ONLY) and matches path.name == work_id or path.name.endswith('-'+work_id). A single filesystem name can never contain '/', so BOTH tests are unsatisfiable for a nested work_id -> archive_dirs is always empty -> phase=archive raises 'no archived run package found' (line 133-137) and the leaked-artifact scan (121-127) silently checks nothing. Every OTHER work_id use in the module is a Path join or substring test and IS slash-safe: 113,117,130 (agent_work/work_id), 150+212 (staged-feedback/work_id), 93+160 (work_id in text), 29 (_entry_block heading match).

Grep over constellation-skills/scripts for split('/') / .name == work_id / endswith('-'+work_id) returns ONLY run_crew.py:936 and verify_agent_feedback.py:79. recover_crews.py takes work_id as a positional CLI arg and calls run_crew.registry_path directly (recover_crews.py:223,229) so it is unaffected; init_work_area/verify_state_note/map_orient all join work_id as a path.

q6.title: Can a NEW shared sibling module actually reach both consumers in an INSTALL, and what wiring does that require?
q6.imperative: fact: read the sibling-import idiom in verify_agent_feedback.py and install_constellation.py SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS / SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES; check which skills bundle each consumer.
q6.finding: FACT, and it is the load-bearing install risk. The sibling-import idiom already exists: verify_agent_feedback.py:12-13 does sys.path.insert(0, Path(__file__).parent) then 'from agent_work_root import durable_root'. install_constellation.py:88-109 SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS expresses exactly this dependency so a sibling cannot be forgotten (the gauge_reader drift it was built for). CRITICAL ASYMMETRY: SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES (143-173) gives 'commander' agent_work_root.py but 'explorer' bundles run_crew.py WITHOUT it — so a new shared module imported by run_crew.py MUST be declared as a companion of BOTH run_crew.py and verify_agent_feedback.py, or the explorer install breaks. The existing companion-closure test (tests/test_install_constellation.py:1250-1279) only covers checklist_engine.py, so nothing would catch the omission today.

q7.title: What archive-directory shapes actually occur on disk for a nested work id?
q7.imperative: fact: inspect real .agent-work/archive names in f1Brainz and the archive imperative text in COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json.

COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json's archive imperative says move .agent-work/<work-id>/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-<work-id>/, which for work_id 'epic-659/665' literally yields the NESTED path .agent-work/archive/2026-07-25-epic-659/665/. Both shapes are therefore live in the wild; the epic-659/665 run hit the failure at exactly this gate and force-waived archive.c1 (grounding: .agent-work/staged-feedback/epic-659/665/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md lines 5-23).

d1.title: DECISION: fix the constellation-skills SOURCE repo (and reinstall), or patch the installed copies under ~/.claude/skills?
d1.imperative: decision: the issue routes the fix upstream; confirm the change target and whether reinstall is in scope for this issue.
d1.finding: DECISION (no human reachable; engagement prompt delegates: 'wherever a step calls for a human decision, record what you would have asked, decide it yourself'). WOULD HAVE ASKED: do we change C:/Programs/constellation-skills (source) and reinstall, or hot-patch ~/.claude/skills? RULING: change the SOURCE repo only. The installed tree is build output of install_constellation.py; a hot-patch is erased by the next install and leaves the defect upstream, which is precisely what the issue routes against ('route to wherever constellation-commander's scripts are maintained'). Reinstall/rollout is NOT part of the code change: it is a post-merge operator step, named in the plan as a handover note, not a gate deliverable. f1Brainz itself gets ZERO source changes from this issue.

d2.title: DECISION: one shared helper module both scripts import, or two independent local patches?
d2.imperative: decision: shared module costs new install-companion wiring; two patches cost duplicated semantics. The issue text already states a preference.
d2.finding: DECISION (same delegation). WOULD HAVE ASKED: one shared module both scripts import, or two independent local patches? RULING: one shared module, scripts/work_id_paths.py. The issue text already rules it ('a single shared work_id-safe parsing/matching helper both scripts import'), and the two-patch form loses the one thing worth having — a single written statement of the work_id contract that a THIRD script can import instead of re-deriving. Accepted cost: new install-companion wiring (q6) plus one more file in every affected bundle. Rejected sub-option: bolting the helpers onto agent_work_root.py — that module is about durable-root resolution, and explorer bundles run_crew.py without it, so reuse would drag an unrelated module into the explorer install.

d3.title: DECISION: which archive-dir naming is canonical for a nested work id, and must the matcher accept more than one shape?
d3.imperative: decision: nested (<date>-epic-N/<issue>) vs flattened (<date>-epic-N-issue); recognizer-accepts-both vs single canonical namer.
d3.finding: DECISION (same delegation). WOULD HAVE ASKED: is the canonical archive dir for a nested work id the NESTED <date>-epic-N/<issue> or a FLATTENED <date>-epic-N-issue, and should the matcher accept both? RULING: the matcher is a RECOGNIZER, not a namer — accept both shapes, and do not legislate a naming convention in this issue. Nested is what the spine's own archive imperative literally produces (q7) and flattened is what commanders actually wrote on disk; a matcher that accepts only one guarantees a second forced waive for whoever picks the other. Match rule: for a work_id of k segments, compare the archive-relative POSIX path (depth k) for equality-or-'-'-suffix, AND the same test against the segment-joined flattening. Separators are normalized (a Windows-authored 'epic-659\665' reads the same as 'epic-659/665').

d4.title: DECISION: does this issue also change doctrine/templates (spine archive imperative, commander-core), or code+tests only?
d4.imperative: decision: bounded code fix vs doctrine statement that a work_id may contain path segments.
d4.finding: DECISION (same delegation). WOULD HAVE ASKED: does #716 also amend doctrine (COMMANDER_SPINE archive imperative, commander-core.md) to state that a work_id may contain path segments? RULING: NO — code + tests + the helper's own docstring contract only. Editing a spine template imperative changes what every future run executes and would need a human at the keyboard; the recognizer-accepts-both ruling (d3) makes the doctrine edit unnecessary for correctness. A doctrine note ('a work_id MAY contain / segments; nested archive dirs are legal') is logged as a triage candidate for the run's triage step instead of smuggled into this fix.

d5.title: DECISION: how much regression protection — targeted unit tests only, or also generalize the installer companion-closure test beyond checklist_engine.py?
d5.imperative: decision: the silent-no-op install failure this guard exists for is exactly the risk a new shared module reintroduces.
d5.finding: DECISION (same delegation). WOULD HAVE ASKED: unit tests only, or also widen the installer companion-closure guard past checklist_engine.py? RULING: BOTH, but the widening stays narrow — extend the runtime-sibling closure test to every script named in SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES (data-driven from the actual imports), not a new bespoke guard. Rationale: this change reintroduces exactly the failure the guard exists for (a bundled script importing a sibling that some bundle omits), and today explorer would ship a run_crew.py whose import raises. Unlike the engine's try/except no-op, a bare import failure here is LOUD — still a broken install, caught only in the field. This is one test-file edit, in the file that already owns the mechanism.

consolidation.summary: PROBLEM STATEMENT (issue-716): Two constellation shared-machinery functions assume a work_id is a single path segment, so this repo's nested Commander-under-Admiral work ids (epic-<N>/<issue>) break them. (1) run_crew.load_registry_for_resume derives work_id as session.split('/')[1], silently truncating to the first segment and pointing --verify-result/--resume/--abandon at the wrong registry. (2) verify_agent_feedback._current_run_archive_dirs matches a directory NAME against a work_id containing '/', which no filesystem name can satisfy, so --phase archive can never find the archived package and its leaked-artifact scan silently checks nothing. Fix = one shared, installed-alongside helper module (work_id_paths.py) holding the work_id contract: an exact session-name inverse and a segment-aware archive-dir recognizer that accepts nested AND flattened dated names. Change lands in the constellation-skills SOURCE repo; f1Brainz gets no source change. Protected intent: never silently resolve to the WRONG work area (fail visibly instead), and never let the archive gate pass vacuously.
